body:
Greptile Summary

 This PR fixes a flaky test by correcting the flush-readiness condition in `TestSubscribeLoop_FlushProvenGapSkipsToRetained`. The old `waitForFlushedFiles` helper returned as soon as the first flush landed (eviction watermark = w0's stop time), allowing w1..w4 to race with `deleteAllLogFiles` and corrupt the test scenario. - Replaces `waitForFlushedFiles` with `waitForFlushedThrough(t, h, h.tsAt(lastSealed, 0))`, blocking until the flush watermark reaches window 4 (the last sealed window), which by the single-channel flush ordering guarantees w0..w3 are already on disk before deletion proceeds. - The old helper is fully removed; the new one is its only call-site, so there is no interface surface change outside this test file.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 Test-only change targeting a single well-understood race condition; no production code is touched. The fix tightens a flush-readiness predicate so that all sealed windows are guaranteed on disk before the deletion step. The single-channel flush ordering is the load-bearing invariant, and it is correctly exploited. No production code changes, no new test logic beyond the corrected wait condition. **Files Needing Attention:** No files require special attention.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | weed/server/filer_subscribe_loop_test.go | Replaces the too-early flush-wait predicate with a stronger one that waits through the last sealed window, eliminating the race with deleteAllLogFiles that caused intermittent 3-of-5 deliveries. |

Sequence Diagram

 ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant T as Test participant LB as LogBuffer participant FQ as FlushQueue participant FS as Filesystem T->>LB: append w0..w5 (seals w0..w4) LB->>FQ: enqueue flush(w0), flush(w1), flush(w2), flush(w3), flush(w4) Note over T: OLD: waitForFlushedFiles returns when flush(w0) lands FQ->>FS: flush(w0) Note over T,FS: w1..w4 still queued — RACE with deleteAllLogFiles Note over T: NEW: waitForFlushedThrough(tsAt(4,0)) waits until flush(w4) lands FQ->>FS: flush(w1) FQ->>FS: flush(w2) FQ->>FS: flush(w3) FQ->>FS: flush(w4) Note over T,FS: All sealed windows on disk — safe to delete T->>FS: deleteAllLogFiles T->>LB: subscribe from 0 → expects 5 retained events ```
